execution.nativeToolBoundary: Native FFmpeg generated only deterministic small source fixtures and independently validated browser outputs; every conversion under test executed through the production browser Wasm pipeline.

avi.video: 640x360 MPEG-4 Part 2, 1:1 sample aspect, 16:9 display aspect, chroma-left
avi.audio: two 48 kHz mono MP3 tracks; AVI retains stream titles but not requested language/default fields

webm.video: 640x360 AV1, 1:1 sample aspect, 16:9 display aspect, limited range, progressive
webm.audio: two 48 kHz mono Opus tracks with eng/spa languages, distinct titles, and 1/0 default dispositions
webm.subtitle: one French default WebVTT track with title

ogg.video: 640x360 Theora, 1:1 sample aspect, 16:9 display aspect, chroma-center
ogg.audio: two 48 kHz mono Vorbis tracks with eng/spa comments and distinct titles; Ogg carries no default dispositions
ogg.generalMetadata: FFmpeg's Ogg muxer represents the requested comment and title fields as per-stream Vorbis/Theora comments, not container tags

sourceFields: audio sample rate and channel count
every representable language, title, comment, and default disposition
WebVTT language, title, and default disposition
payloads: each compressed video packet stream matches exactly
each of the two compressed audio packet streams matches exactly
the WebVTT subtitle packet stream matches exactly
assertions.warnings: none for any of the three fully compatible source topologies

destinationOutcomes.aviToMatroska: all MPEG-4 Part 2 and both MP3 streams, source-present fields, stream titles, title/comment, and exact payloads retained
destinationOutcomes.webmToMatroska: all AV1, both Opus, and WebVTT streams plus languages, titles, dispositions, general metadata, chapter timing, and exact payloads retained
destinationOutcomes.oggToMatroska: Theora and both Vorbis streams plus per-stream languages/titles/comments, geometry, audio layout, zero-default semantics, and exact payloads retained

diagnosticHistory.finding: The conversion behavior passed, but the follow-up reproducibility audit found changing WebM SegmentUID and Ogg stream serial values, so this run was not accepted as deterministic-fixture evidence.

diagnosticHistory.attempt: bit-exact fixture generation and repeatability audit
diagnosticHistory.result: all three source byte sizes and SHA-256 hashes matched across two consecutive generations
diagnosticHistory.resolution: The WebM and Ogg fixture recipes now use FFmpeg +bitexact muxing; AVI was already byte-repeatable.
Exact packet/decode, field, warning, bounded-I/O, queue, and Wasm assertions all passed with deterministic genuine source containers.

diagnosticHistory.result: the old complex Matroska file copied to a .webm filename was removed from the active browser suite
diagnosticHistory.resolution: WebM coverage now depends only on a standards-compliant AV1/Opus/WebVTT WebM source; the historical alias is not counted as genuine WebM evidence.

scope: This closes complex AVI-, genuine WebM-, and genuine Ogg-origin field and payload mappings for every currently compatible public destination, which is Matroska for each family. M-03 remains partial only for resolving attached-picture disposition behavior across applicable video-container profiles.
